cards.explanation: The answer is war and battle. David says the LORD "…trains my hands for war, my fingers for battle." (Psalm 144:1) Notice who the trainer is, friends. David doesn't brag about his own skills, he gives the credit to his Rock. I've pressed thousands of cookies and I'd never claim my mustache learned it alone.

The answer is take refuge. David says the LORD is "…my shield, in whom I take refuge…" (Psalm 144:2) Taking refuge means running TO something safe, friends. When a blazing hot tray comes out of my oven, I dive behind the cooling rack, but David picked a much better place to hide.

The answer is why He would think of man. David asks, "O LORD, what is man, that You regard him, the son of man that You think of him?" (Psalm 144:3) I think he's amazed that the LORD thinks of us at all. I think that's a good place to land after all that talk of fortresses.

The answer is to scatter them in defeat. David asks, "Flash forth Your lightning and scatter them; shoot Your arrows and rout them." (Psalm 144:6) To rout someone means to beat them so they run, friends. David is asking the LORD for a full win.

The answer is False. David says the foreigners' "…mouths speak falsehood, whose right hands are deceitful." (Psalm 144:8) So they speak lies, not truth. And he says their right hands are deceitful, so even a handshake from them can't be trusted.

The answer is that David will sing Him a new song. He says, "I will sing to You a new song, O God; on a harp of ten strings I will make music to You…" (Psalm 144:9) He's in the middle of asking for rescue, and he says he will sing. That's a lot of music promised in the middle of a prayer, friends.

The answer is True. David sings to "…Him who gives victory to kings, who frees His servant David from the deadly sword." (Psalm 144:10) Notice he calls himself His servant, friends. The song goes to the One who gives the victory and frees him from the sword.

The answer is our sons. David says, "Then our sons will be like plants nurtured in their youth…" (Psalm 144:12) Think of a plant that gets watered and looked after while it's young, friends. That's the picture, and it's a sweet one.

The answer is a palace. David says, "…our daughters like corner pillars carved to adorn a palace." (Psalm 144:12) To adorn means to decorate, friends. So these pillars are carved to make a palace beautiful.
The answer is no breach at all. David says, "There will be no breach in the walls…" (Psalm 144:14) A breach is a break in a wall, friends. In his picture, the walls have none.

The answer is False. David says there will be "…no breach in the walls, no going into captivity, and no cry of lament in our streets." (Psalm 144:14) So the statement says the opposite of what David says, friends. In his picture, there's no going into captivity.

The answer is blessed. David ends with, "Blessed are the people of whom this is so; blessed are the people whose God is the LORD." (Psalm 144:15) He opened the psalm with "Blessed be the LORD…" and he closes on blessed too, friends. It starts and ends in the same good place.
